 Law-enforcement authorities in Cape Town gear-up for festive season
 TygerBurger
 | 
 29 Oct 2026 
 The Voortrekker Road Corridor Improvement District (VRCID) and City of Cape Town’s Metro Police, Law Enforcement and Traffic Services held a joint operation in Parow.

 With the festive season just around the corner law-enforcement authorities in Cape Town are gearing themselves up to ensure they are able to cope with any situation they may encounter.
 In Parow this week the Voortrekker Road Corridor Improvement District (VRCID) along with the City of Cape Town’s Metro Police, Law Enforcement and Traffic Services conducted a joint operation in an attempt to strengthen public safety and as a show of visibility. The operation was conducted in the central business district (CBD).
 Luané de Vries, VRCID spokesperson, said the operation on Wednesday 28 October formed part of proactive festive season preparations aimed at addressing crime, by-law infringements and other public safety concerns before the traditionally busy holiday period.
 During the operation, officers conducted stop-and-search activities targeting drugs and illegal substances, while vehicle checkpoints focused on checking drivers’ licences and outstanding traffic fines.
 Teams also attended to illegal trading and engaged with individuals sleeping rough in public spaces, while maintaining a visible presence throughout the CBD, De Vries said.
 ALSO READ: Drugs and jamming equipment seized during Parow safety operation 
 Early start
 According to Derek Bock, VRCID chief operating officer, the decision to begin festive season operations early is deliberate.
 “We don’t want to wait until December to start preparing for the festive season. Our intention is to establish a strong, visible presence well in advance so that residents, businesses, commuters and visitors know that the VRCID, police, Metro Police, Law Enforcement and other enforcement partners are active in the area.
 “Visibility plays an important role in crime prevention. When people see officers patrolling, conducting inspections and responding to concerns, it sends a clear message that public safety remains a priority and that unlawful activities will not simply be overlooked.
 “By working together and starting early, we aim to create a safer and better-managed environment for everyone who lives, works, trades or travels through the CBD.” 
 Bock explained that the festive season typically brings increased pedestrian and vehicle activity, placing additional pressure on public spaces and creating opportunities for criminal activity.
 He emphasised that coordinated operations allow different enforcement agencies to combine their resources, share information and address a wider range of concerns during a single operation.
 “Public safety is not something that any one organisation can manage in isolation. The strength of these operations lies in the cooperation between the different teams, each contributing its expertise and resources towards a common objective.
 “Our approach is not only about responding when incidents occur, but also about identifying potential problems early, maintaining visibility and taking preventative action wherever possible.”
 The VRCID continues to work closely with the police, City enforcement departments and other partners to support public safety, urban management and social development initiatives within its operational area, he said.
 Businesses and public
 Bock also encouraged businesses and members of the public to play their part by remaining vigilant and reporting suspicious activity.
 “An effective public safety network depends on more than the officers on the ground. Businesses, residents and the public are important partners in helping us identify concerns and respond appropriately. We encourage everyone to remain alert and report incidents rather than assuming someone else will do so.”
 The VRCID’s 24-hour Control Room can be contacted on 072 792 7168 to report suspicious activity or request assistance within its operational area.
 Provincial festive safety season
 The Western Cape police also launched their Safer Festive Season operations this month. The launch, which took place on Wednesday 21 October at the Nyanga Rugby Stadium was attended by Acting Minister of Police, Feroz Cachalia.
 The provincial police said joint policing operations will be intensified this festive season, with increased police visibility and targeted interventions aimed at ensuring the safety and security of residents and visitors.
 About 175 new vehicles were also handed over to six police districts in the province at the launch, to bolster operational activities.
